subject: Marketplace entitlements - edge cases and integration asks
messages:
From: Suresh Rao <suresh.rao@cloudbridge.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Marketplace entitlements - edge cases and integration asks

Hi Marcus,

Thanks again for taking the call earlier. Per our discussion we dug into a few customer scenarios that hit edge-case behaviour when provisioning Redwood through Azure Marketplace. I attached an initial entitlement matrix and our integration spec. The main items we need clarity on: 

- Metering/entitlement mapping: when an account purchases both a hosted+dedicated package, how does Redwood expect to map meter IDs to tenant orgs?
- Seat transfers: large customers often move seats between sub-orgs; is there an API your team exposes for revoking/reattaching entitlements without forcing a new deployment?
- Trial to commit conversion: what metadata do you rely on to reconcile a marketplace trial converted via Azure with an existing Redwood account?

High-level ask: can we get a short doc or decision on the above by end of week so CloudBridge can finalize the Marketplace listing flow? Also including Emily from Azure who asked to be looped in.

Attachments: entitlement-matrix.csv, cloudbridge-integration-specs.pdf

Regards,
Suresh Rao
Partner Lead — CloudBridge
suresh.rao@cloudbridge.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Suresh Rao <suresh.rao@cloudbridge.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Emily Tan <emily.tan@azuremarketplace.microsoft.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace entitlements - edge cases and integration asks

Thanks Suresh — good summary. Looping in Tessa (Product Partnerships) for the technical/roadmap context and Priyom for billing/procurement implications. Quick answers below, then I’ll follow up with a short doc and an action plan.

1) Metering/entitlement mapping:
- Short: we use a marketplace order id -> account mapping in our entitlement service. We can accept up to two external meter IDs per account (hosted + dedicated). If both exist, Redwood will prefer the most recent active meter by purchase date.
- Caveat: customers that split purchases across Azure orders can produce duplicates; recommend CloudBridge reconcile at purchase time and pass a preferred "primary_meter_id" field.

2) Seat transfers:
- We don’t currently have a self-serve seat-transfer API. Transfers are handled via a backend job tied to the entitlement id. Roadmap: Tessa, can you confirm ETA for exposing a transfer endpoint (public API) or a partner-only admin API?

3) Trial -> commit conversion:
- We use an enrollment token the marketplace provides; we map that token to the Redwood user by email+azure_tenant_id. If the email domain matches an existing tenant we merge automatically; otherwise we create a new tenant and surface a manual reconciliation flag in the Console.

Action items: I’ll draft a 1-pager with the definitive guidance and open a GH issue for the API work. Proposed owners: Marcus (doc), Tessa (API spec & ETA), Priyom (billing reconciliation).

Thanks,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Enterprise Partnerships — Redwood Inference

+ a quick legal note on procurement/contracting:
- If CloudBridge is listing Redwood as a transactable product in their Marketplace offering, we need a Marketplace Addendum signed (template attached in internal repo).
- For seat transfers that touch multiple legal entities, procurement will require a statement of work or amendment. Priyom — please prepare an outline of the billing amendment we’d ask for in these cases.

Suresh — happy to share the addendum template; we'll need to know whether CloudBridge wants Redwood to be the transacting vendor or listed as a reseller (this affects tax/PO flow).

—Laura

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>

On Tue, Jun 22, 2026 at 10:05 AM Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai> wrote:
> 1) Metering/entitlement mapping:
> - Short: we use a marketplace order id -> account mapping in our entitlement service. We can accept up to two external meter IDs per account (hosted + dedicated). If both exist, Redwood will prefer the most recent active meter by purchase date.

Thanks for the summary — adding technical context and a proposed short-term workaround we can implement immediately:

- Short-term (2 weeks): accept an optional primary_meter_id and partner_signature header in the provisioning call. If provided, our provisioning service will bind that meter id as authoritative and skip duplicate detection. This avoids requiring immediate changes from CloudBridge customers.
- Mid-term (quarter roadmap): expose a partner-admin API to perform seat transfers and bulk entitlement rebinds. This will be gated on partner onboarding (RBAC + audit logs).
- Notes: this requires changes to the provisioning lambda and one small DB migration; estimate ~3 engineer-weeks. Priyom — I'll need guidance on audit log retention for the partner-admin flows.

I can draft an API spec by Friday. Marcus — do you want me to include sample request/response payloads for the primary_meter_id path?

—Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Product Partnerships — Redwood Inference
tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
